Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 1:

﴿When the sun is wrapped up﴾, meaning it is rolled up and its light is taken away.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 81, verse 2:

﴿And when the stars fall, becoming dark﴾ they plunge down and drop onto the earth.
﴿And when the mountains are set in motion﴾ they are taken away from the face of the earth, and they become scattered dust.

And when the pregnant she-camels (al-'ishar) are abandoned ﴿عُطِّلَتْ﴾ left without a herdsman or without milking, because of the calamity that has befallen them, even though they had no property more precious to them than these.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 5:

﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ — they will be brought together after the Resurrection so that retribution may be exacted for some of them from others; then they will become dust.

{Wa-idhā al-biḥāru sujjirat} — with the lightened and the intensified readings: they were set ablaze, so they became fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 10:

﴿And when the pages﴾ — the pages of deeds — ﴿are unfolded﴾, with the light and the intensive forms (nushirat, read with takhfif and tashdid), meaning they are opened and spread out.

﴿And when the sky is stripped away﴾ it is removed from its places, as the hide is stripped from the sheep.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 14:

﴿Every soul will know﴾ every soul, at the time of these mentioned events, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿what it has brought forth﴾ of good and evil.
﴿So I swear﴾ the "lā" is extra (*zā'ida*, a redundant particle), meaning "by the Khunnas."

﴿Al-jawari al-kunnas﴾ are the five planets: Zuhal (Saturn), al-Mushtari (Jupiter), al-Marrikh (Mars), al-Zuhara (Venus), and Utarid (Mercury). Takhnus, with the nun pointed with a ḍamma, means they recede in their course, going backward, whereas we see the star at the end of the zodiac sign, then it returns to its beginning. And takniss, with the nun pointed with a kasra, means they enter their kinas (lairs), that is, they set in the places where they set.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 21:

﴿Obeyed there⁠﴾ — the angels obey him in the heavens. ﴿Trustworthy⁠﴾ — over the revelation.
﴿And your companion﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), coordinated (ʿuṭifa) with "indeed it" (innahu) up to the end of what is sworn to, ﴿is not a madman﴾ as you claimed.
﴿And he had certainly seen him﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ) saw Jibril (Gabriel) in his form in which he was created, ﴿on the clear horizon﴾, the manifest one, and it is the highest part on the side of the east.

and he is not one who withholds (ﷺ) knowledge of the unseen... 

Let me translate carefully:

﴿Wa-ma huwa﴾ — "And he is not" — Muhammad (ﷺ) — ﴿ʿalā al-ghayb﴾ — "concerning the unseen," meaning what was hidden of the Revelation and the news of the heaven — ﴿bi-ḍanīn﴾ — "accused," i.e., one who is suspected; and in another reading, with the ḍād (bi-ḍaníin), i.e., "stingy," so that he would withhold something of it.

**Translation:**

And he is not ﴿ʿalā al-ghayb﴾ — (Muhammad (ﷺ)) — concerning the unseen, meaning what was hidden of the Revelation and the news of the heaven, ﴿bi-ḍanīn﴾, i.e., not accused (bi-muttahamin). In another reading it is read with a ḍād (bi-ḍanīn), meaning stingy (bi-bakhīl), so that he would withhold something of it.

**Glossary:** *al-ghayb* (the unseen); *ḍanīn* (one who is accused, or in the other reading, one who is stingy).

And it is not the word of a devil, stoned (rajim).

Note: the Qur'an is not the word of an accursed Satan (shaytan), the eavesdropper (mustariq al-sam') who is stoned (marjum), with the commentary's gloss the word of the "devil" refers to the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 26:

﴿Where then are you going?﴾ By which path will you proceed in your denial of the Qur'an and your turning away from it?

In the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 27:

﴿In it is not﴾ (i.e., "in" here means "it is not") ﴿but a reminder﴾ (ʿiẓah, an admonition) ﴿to the worlds﴾, namely mankind and the jinn.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 28:

﴿For whoever among you wills to go straight﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "for all the worlds," with the preposition repeated, ﴿to go straight﴾ by following the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 81, verse 29:

﴿And you will not will﴾ steadfastness upon the truth, ﴿except that Allah wills, Lord of the worlds﴾ — the creation — your steadfastness upon it.
